name: Tacrolimus
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: Immediate-release (twice daily) and prolonged-release (once daily) tacrolimus are not interchangeable mg for mg; do not switch without specialist conversion and trough monitoring (label 2.1, 5.3). Doses shown are for immediate-release capsules.
0.2 mg/kg/day in 2 doses; trough 7–20 ng/mL months 1–3, 5–15 ng/mL months 4–12

usual_adult_dose.indication: Kidney transplant (with mycophenolate and IL-2 receptor antagonist)
usual_adult_dose.dose: 0.1 mg/kg/day in 2 doses; trough 4–11 ng/mL months 1–12
0.10 to 0.15 mg/kg/day in 2 doses; trough 5–20 ng/mL

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Strong CYP3A inhibitors (azoles, clarithromycin, protease inhibitors, nelfinavir), grapefruit
key_interactions.effect: Higher tacrolimus levels; nephrotoxicity, QT prolongation (label).
key_interactions.action: Avoid nelfinavir and grapefruit; otherwise monitor troughs and reduce dose.

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Mild or moderate CYP3A inhibitors (diltiazem, verapamil, nifedipine, fluconazole, erythromycin, amiodarone)
key_interactions.action: Monitor troughs; reduce dose if needed.

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Nephrotoxic drugs (aminoglycosides, amphotericin B, cyclosporine; NSAIDs: clinical)
key_interactions.effect: Additive nephrotoxicity (label 5.5: caution with nephrotoxic drugs; do not use with cyclosporine, 2.1).
key_interactions.action: Avoid cyclosporine together; monitor creatinine with others.

common: Abnormal kidney function, hypertension, tremor, headache
Hyperglycemia, new-onset diabetes, hyperkalemia, hypomagnesemia, hyperlipemia
serious: Thrombotic microangiopathy (with sirolimus), pure red cell aplasia

contraindications: Injection: hypersensitivity to polyoxyl 60 hydrogenated castor oil (HCO-60)

pk.half_life_eskd: Similar to normal in kidney impairment and dialysis (label)
pk.excretion_renal_pct: Under 1% unchanged in urine; mainly feces

sources.citation: Astellas Pharma US, Inc. (2023). PROGRAF (tacrolimus) capsules, injection and granules [Prescribing information; US FDA-approved label, NDA050708, set ID 7f667de1-9dfa-4bd6-8ba0-15ee2d78873b, version effective August 25, 2023]. DailyMed, U.S. National Library of Medicine.
